sources: recreation.gov public search API per-site catalog for facility 249999 (catx.py), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 2026 peak season (May 1 - Sep 13): standard site $10, marked double site $20. Group shelters with their own campsites: Lewis & Clark (15 sites) $170, York (10) $130, Hellgate Bay (5) $90 a night.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/249999/rates (2026-05-01 to 2026-09-13 Peak: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 10, STANDARD NONELECTRIC double 20, group shelters 90/130/170) + notices, read 2026-10-22

values.note: 14 nights in a rolling 30 days. Booking opens 6 months ahead; no cutoff before arrival. Sites must be occupied each night; no-shows cancelled after the third night. Check-in 5 pm, check-out 4 pm.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/249999 (facility_rules reservationWindow 6 Months, reservationCutOff 0, maxStay 14 days 'Rolling 30 Days'; notices 'Campsites must be occupied each night', 'No show reservations are subject to cancellation after the third night', 'Check in time is 5pm. Check out is 4pm.') + https://www.usbr.gov/gp/recreation/cfrrec.html ('campsites for Court Sheriff and Hellgate Campgrounds can be reserved at recreation.gov'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 69 standard sites (one tent-only) plus 3 group shelters with 15/10/5 campsites. Catalog vehicle lengths run 20-120 ft: most 30-60 ft, 5 sites 100-120 ft, 2 at 20 ft. One camping unit per site unless marked double.

sites.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/249999 ('Hellgate Campground consists of 69 campsites and 3 Group Use shelters', 'one camping unit is permitted per site unless marked as a double campsite') + recreation.gov per-site catalog (69 standard sites, max vehicle length 20-120 ft), read 2026-10-22

hookups.source: recreation.gov per-site catalog for 249999 (all 69 standard sites typed STANDARD NONELECTRIC, no electric attribute) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/249999 (notice 'No electrical source for camp trailers or RVs is available at shelters'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Two boat ramps, boat-trailer parking and day-use picnic sites; campground host. Generators not allowed during quiet hours (10 pm - 7 am).

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/249999 (amenities 'Accessible Flush Toilets', 'Accessible Vault Toilets', 'Drinking Water', 'Boat Ramp', 'Host'; 'Hellgate Boat Ramp and Day Use Area provides two boat ramps'; quiet-hours notice), read 2026-10-22

note: Bureau of Reclamation campground on a long point on Canyon Ferry Lake, 30 miles east of Helena on MT-284, in an open valley between the Big Belt and Elkhorn ranges (a narrow riparian canopy gives partial shade along the shore); boat access, plus three group shelters with their own sites. Fees only from the first weekend of May to the second weekend of September. Since March 25, 2026 a shoreline protection project has temporarily closed some Hellgate campsites (usbr.gov Canyon Ferry page). --Claude
summary: rec.gov record, rates and catalog confirm $10 standard sites (2026), 69 sites to 120 ft, no electric; added recreation.gov booking (6-month window, 14 nights in 30), flush and vault toilets, drinking water. USBR's Canyon Ferry page says a shoreline project (from March 25, 2026) has temporarily closed SOME Hellgate campsites (partial, so in the note, not status). Not stated: season, fcfs. Note trimmed of restated values ('25-120 ft' was also wrong: the catalog has 20-ft sites).
flags: Website is the recreation.gov listing; the operator's page is USBR's Canyon Ferry Reservoir page https://www.usbr.gov/gp/mtao/canyonferry/ (recreation info https://www.usbr.gov/gp/recreation/cfrrec.html).
max_rig_ft 120 rests on 5 catalog sites at 100-120 ft; plausible lakeside pads but unusual, so worth a glance.
